chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, does the pregnant woman sometimes menstruate?' He said, 'Yes, and that is because the child in the belly of its mother, its sustenance is the blood. So, sometimes there is excess from it, it is repelled. So when it is repelled, the Salat is Prohibited upon her.' And in another report, '(He said): When it was like that, the birth would be delayed'.
ai.seo_question: Does a pregnant woman menstruate and does it affect her prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the physiological basis for *hayd* in pregnancy, noting that the fetus's sustenance is blood, and excess may be expelled, rendering the woman ritually impure and exempt from prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that menstrual blood in pregnancy is treated as *hayd* for the purpose of prayer prohibition, distinguishing it from *istihadha* (irregular bleeding). The mention of delayed childbirth underscores the physical toll of this process, reinforcing the practical application of ritual purity laws during pregnancy.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Does the pregnant woman menstruate sometimes?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, and that is because the child in the belly of its mother, its sustenance is the blood. So, sometimes there is excess from it, it is repelled. So when it is repelled, the Salaat is Prohibited upon her’. And in another report, ‘(Heasws said): ‘When it was like that, the birth would be delayed’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a pregnant woman, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, can such woman experience Hayd (menses)? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, because the child’s food in mother’s womb is blood. It (blood) may exceed the amount of food for the child. It (the excess) is then repelled. When this happens, Salah (prayer) becomes unlawful for her.’”
In another Hadith it is said that it causes a birth delay.
